results.question: Which country takes the largest share of Sri Lanka's tea exports?
results.answer: In 2024, Iraq was the largest importer of Sri Lankan tea, accounting for 10.9% of the total export value, which amounted to USD 149,621,564 out of a total of USD 1,373,467,019. Sri Lanka exported tea to 145 different markets, demonstrating a diversified export base with a Herfindahl concentration index of 0.05, indicating low market concentration. Additionally, the United Arab Emirates emerged as the fastest-growing market for Sri Lankan tea, with a compound annual growth rate of 31.6% from 2020 to 2024.

results.question: How fast have cinnamon exports grown over the last five years?
results.answer: Cinnamon exports from Sri Lanka have contracted at an average rate of 0.2% per year over the last five years, reaching a total export value of USD 214,425,881 in 2024. Mexico is the largest market, accounting for 38.4% of this export value. Honduras, however, has been the fastest-growing destination for Sri Lankan cinnamon, with an annual growth rate of 7.7% during the same period. There is no available data on cinnamon-producing districts, which limits the ability to assess export growth at a more granular level.

results.question: How concentrated are Sri Lanka's rubber export destinations?
results.answer: Sri Lanka's rubber export destinations are relatively diversified. In 2024, the country exported USD 25,787,076 worth of rubber to 36 different markets. India emerged as the fastest-growing destination for Sri Lankan rubber from 2020 to 2024, with an annual growth rate of 18.1%.
